action_summary: Round 7 repointed eight repair predicates to pass and inverted the gate tests, but every one of those tests asks the gate to REJECT, and a gate that rejects everything satisfies all of them. This is measured, not argued: reducing ast.Add:[ast.Sub, ast.Mult] to ast.Add:[ast.Sub] in the patch-search adapter removes the repair for the canonical injected-operator defect class, and all 11 pre-existing gate tests still PASS while the added positive control FAILS 2. The existing success-side test feeds a hand-written pass=True dict to _check_expect, so it checks the evaluator and not any result a producer produced. Added REPAIRABLE_FIXTURE (return x + x, reachable because Add->Mult is in _BINOP_SWAPS), run_positive_control(), and six tests that execute real adapters: 5/5 solvers find and verify the repair, the live gate accepts 5/5 and rejects 0, and the two acceptance controllers correctly fail closed where the legacy transport predicate accepted both. The adapter used for the falsification was restored; no adapter byte and no registry line ships in this change. Claims no capability progress.

obs_solution.losing_routes_reason: Re-implementing the eight repoints would have duplicated merged work and produced a 24k-line reformat. A new verification framework would replace loaders that already run every adapter. Repointing the ninth without a real receipt would substitute one unverified acceptance for another.

obs_verification.synthetic_verification_necessity: The instrument was itself falsified twice before being trusted. Breaking the mutation grammar: 11 existing tests passed, the new control failed 2. Pointing the live predicate at an absent field: 3 new tests failed. The fixture's reachability and its initial failure are executed directly with no adapter and no predicate involved, so neither a grammar bug nor an evaluator bug can satisfy them.
